assertion.statement: Over Q the literal recipe preserves conjunction by sums of squares and disjunction by products, with private witness blocks and globally active fixed rational-constant equations.
assertion.objects: The actual scalar nodes, template calls, parameter substitutions and private consecutive witness blocks of P_star.
assertion.hypotheses: Rational coefficients and witnesses; private blocks do not identify unrelated variables; rational constants p/q have q!=0.
assertion.quantifiers: Every actual recipe call and every rational assignment of its free parameters.
assertion.parameter_range: Finite sums and products in the fixed recipe; Q is ordered and is an integral domain.
assertion.uniformity: The same fixed recipe and guard apply to every allowed input.
assertion.constants: The cached P0 coordinates satisfy8g0=1641,4g1=-15465,32g2=87483 globally.
assertion.normalizations: All arithmetic is in Q; sums of squares use its usual ordering and products its integral-domain property.
assertion.exceptional_cases: An entire inactive product branch may have arbitrary private witnesses, but fixed equations within an active callee are never discarded. Inversion is enforced by uv=1.
assertion.limit_order: Fix the literal construction and its parameters before evaluating an input; retain the separate incoming template and cutoff proofs.

assertion.statement: The finite product guard rejects every false canonical triple in[-T,T]^3 and is invertible at every true canonical multiplication triple.
assertion.objects: Fifteen canonical code coordinates, positive denominator product D_abc, squared-distance factor g_abc for each false bounded triple, and their finite product.
assertion.hypotheses: Canonical code injectivity and the fixed integer cutoff T. The separate height/box argument must put any false accepted triple in this bounded list.
assertion.quantifiers: Every false triple in the listed finite box and every true canonical triple tested by the guard.
assertion.parameter_range: Integer indices and rational point-code coordinates; the finite product uses exactly the prescribed false triples.
assertion.uniformity: The same fixed recipe and guard apply to every allowed input.
assertion.constants: The actual T and D_abc are fixed before testing inputs; no new cutoff estimate is supplied here.
assertion.normalizations: All arithmetic is in Q; sums of squares use its usual ordering and products its integral-domain property.
assertion.exceptional_cases: A false listed triple has its own zero factor. A true triple differs from every false triple and each squared-distance factor is positive. Pole completeness is not needed for this guard argument.
assertion.limit_order: Fix the literal construction and its parameters before evaluating an input; retain the separate incoming template and cutoff proofs.
